questions.question: Describe biological and cognitive explanations of depression and evaluate each one.

points.text: Biological: genetics (twin studies show heritability), low serotonin/noradrenaline (supported by SSRI effectiveness). Cognitive: Beck's negative triad (negative self, world, future views maintain depression), Seligman's learned helplessness (uncontrollable outcomes lead to hopelessness). questions.question: Compare SSRI medication with CBT as treatments for depression.

points.text: SSRIs: increase serotonin, effective for 60-70% of patients, quick to prescribe, but side effects and treat symptoms not causes. CBT: challenges negative thoughts, teaches skills for long-term management, no side effects, but requires effort and time, therapist availability is limited. questions.question: Evaluate whether depression is best explained as a biological or a psychological condition.

points.text: Depression is best explained by an interaction of both: genetic vulnerability (biological) may be triggered by life events (social), which then activate negative thinking patterns (cognitive). The diathesis-stress model integrates biological predisposition with environmental triggers. Neither explanation alone fully accounts for depression - a biopsychosocial approach is most comprehensive.
